newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares depressed on political worries.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares depressed on political worries.

text.p: Jordanian stock fell 0.20 percent on Tuesday with lack of institutional and investor demand depressing trade worsened by renewed uncertainty over Middle East peace, dealers said.
"The reports of a crisis in Middle East peace talks has cast its shadow on the market which depressed it further... with weak liquidity and few orders," said broker Ibrahim Odeh.
Odeh said some limited demand on leading bluechips helped buttress the market, which saw across-the-board declines, from further slides.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 0.31 points to 155.42 points in low turnover of 404,430 dinars ($571,228).
Most of the larger deals ranged between 20,000 to 30,000 dinars in generally thin trade with minimal buying impetus.
Investor interest, in the absence of major institutional and outside purchases, appears to be focusing on blue chips which are expected to report healthy 1996 earnings, brokers said.

Renewed uncertainty over the fate of Middle East peace adds to investor worries about the fate of $120 million worth of orders won by Jordanian firms under the U.N. "oil-for-food" deal because of approval delays by the sanctions committee.

Many industrial firms are pinning hopes on Iraq exports to boost performance. Recent stock purchases in major drug firms in particular have been motivated by market expectations of better 1997 results on the back of extra export orders to the Iraqi market.
Growing doubts about the government's seriousness in implementing its privatisation pledge has also kept some investors on the sidelines, dealers say.
Selling pressure on leading Arab Bank sent the stock 1.00 dinar lower to 262 dinars, helping drag the market lower.

Jordan National Bank, the second busiest stock traded in small deals not exceeding 35,000 dinars, rose a modest 0.02 dinars to 1.96. Jordan Cement Factories rose 0.01 dinars to 3.50 in trade worth 23,751 dinars.
Only nine stocks rose against 20 losers on Tuesday, while nine traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 most-traded shares on the exchange shed 0.12 percent to 81.44 points, 2.24 percent down from the start of the year.
